A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same code-reasoning survey. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching the renumbered benchmark tables.

before.justification: Section 6 presents the survey's own comparative data analysis of published benchmark scores, producing cross-study rankings and observations. The underlying measurements come from prior papers; no new model experiments are reported.

after.justification: v3 retains the original cross-study analysis and adds calculated comparison margins in Appendix A.5. These are analytical results produced by the survey using measurements attributed to prior papers.

M1.justification: The survey introduces no new algorithm or model in v3. Its reasoning families and surveyed procedures remain the same; revised technique annotations and explanations do not establish changes to the underlying methods.

E1.justification: The benchmark inventory and coverage represented in the results tables remain unchanged. The additional HumanEval, HumanEval+, and GPT-4o MBPP comparisons plotted in v3 use coverage and scores already present in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 3–9 and v3 Tables 5–11 retain the same comparison methods and model entries. The expanded inference-scaling figure reuses the CodeTree versus Revisiting Self-Debugging pair already compared in Section 6.4.

E3.justification: Both versions synthesize published results by matching base models without normalizing other experimental conditions. The corrected pass@5 and resolved-rate chart labels agree with metrics already specified in v2 Tables 4 and 5; they do not establish a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Neither version introduces ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or original error studies. The added margins and expanded performance figure elaborate the existing benchmark comparisons rather than introduce a distinct supplementary test.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates are added. v3 discusses their absence in source papers; its new percentage-point margins are descriptive differences, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The seven benchmark tables retain their numerical scores, but Appendix A.5 newly reports pairwise margins. Section 6.4 also newly identifies mixed findings: with GPT-4o, Revisiting Self-Debugging exceeds CodeTree on HumanEval+ (87.8 versus 86.0), while three other comparisons favor CodeTree. These underlying scores already appeared in v2.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The benchmark metric definitions remain unchanged; the additional qualifications concern interpretation rather than mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a dedicated survey, reasoning taxonomy, benchmark synthesis, and research agenda. The main claim that code-specific reasoning signals are associated with better performance remains.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the six observations as suggestive findings on particular benchmarks and treats inference scaling versus self-refinement as unresolved after acknowledging the HumanEval+ reversal. Section 8.1 expands cross-paper validity threats, Section 8 adds limitations concerning closed systems and cost comparisons, and hypothesis-based calls to action receive explicit qualifications.

D1.justification: Section 2 newly discloses search dates, additional keywords and venues, screening steps, and an exception covering training with generated reasoning data. Figure 2 supplies selection counts. The surveyed-paper repository pointer also changes. These additions document the survey process rather than establish new model experiments.

R1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds detailed justifications for comparisons with existing surveys, and Table 2 revises some component attributions, including those for Revisiting Self-Debugging and S*. The GPT-4o system-card citation is removed. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 expands selected methodology, comparison, and limitations passages, adds an appendix roadmap and subsection organization, and corrects terminology and cross-references. Most explanatory text and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual documentation is substantially expanded: v3 adds a selection-flow diagram and two multipage tables, extends the inference-scaling chart, reformats the technique matrix, and adds publication-status annotations to the taxonomy. It also corrects metric axes, revises captions, and changes typography and figure placement throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the survey easier to assess through fuller selection documentation, explicit comparison margins, and clearer metric labels. Its acknowledgment of mixed inference-scaling results and cross-paper confounders improves interpretive restraint. The gains are limited: the underlying evidence remains unchanged, and new inconsistencies remain, notably Appendix Table 4 assigning Yang et al. partial coverage where Table 1 marks absence.
